messages.content:
TASK: Make routines of useful scraping APIs from the Premier League website

Start by analyzing the exploration summaries. Then:
1. Call plan_routines to declare what routines to build
2. Dispatch experiments for shared dependencies (auth, navigation)
3. Work through routines by priority
4. Call mark_complete when all routines are addressed

Use dispatch_experiment to send experiments to workers, then record_finding to log what you learned.

specs.description: Fetch Premier League standings table for a given competition and season from Pulselive API.
Fetch fixtures/matches for a given competition, season, and matchweek from Pulselive API.
Fetch list of teams for a given competition and season from Pulselive API.
Given a team id, fetch core team data, metadata, form, next fixture, and promo/content items.
Given a player id and season, fetch player profile and season statistics for a competition.
Given a match id, fetch match events and lineups.
Search Premier League content (articles/videos) with filters like contentTypes, pagination, and flags.
Fetch playlist content items given a playlist id.
Fetch detailed metadata for a specific video asset by id.
Fetch broadcasting events schedule filtered by date range and page size.

arguments.hypothesis: Core Pulselive standings endpoint is fully public and can be called directly via HTTPS GET without auth or special headers.
arguments.rationale: Network exploration shows repeated unauthenticated GETs to https://sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com/api/v5/competitions/8/seasons/2025/standings with no Authorization or cookies. We need to confirm this holds in a fresh browser context and whether any required headers (e.g. Origin, Referer, User-Agent) matter.
arguments.prompt:
1. Use browser_navigate to open https://www.premierleague.com/en/ just to establish a realistic origin context.
2. Then, using browser_eval_js, run a fetch to "https://sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com/api/v5/competitions/8/seasons/2025/standings" with method GET and no custom headers (let the browser send defaults). Capture and return:
   - HTTP status
   - Any CORS errors or exceptions
   - A truncated (first 2KB) JSON body if the response is OK.
3. If the fetch fails due to CORS, retry by:
   a) Navigating directly to the API URL with browser_navigate and capturing the raw response body text.
   b) If that still fails, use capture_search_transactions with a query for "standings" to pull the exact recorded request, then use browser_cdp_command (Network.enable + Page.navigate or Fetch.enable) to replicate the working request as closely as possible and capture the JSON response.
Return a concise report of what worked, including final method used and any required headers or preconditions.
arguments.output_description: Report confirming whether the standings endpoint is publicly callable, including method used, status code, any CORS behavior, and sample of JSON payload.

arguments.hypothesis: Pulselive matches API can return fixtures for a given competition, season, and matchweek using only public GET requests with query parameters (no auth).
arguments.rationale: Network exploration shows repeated GETs to https://sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com/api/v2/matches and to the more specific /api/v1/competitions/8/seasons/2025/matchweeks/27/matches endpoint, all without Authorization headers. We need to confirm how to parameterize matchweek-based fixture queries in a fresh browser context and whether CORS or required headers differ from the standings endpoint.
arguments.prompt:
1. Use browser_navigate to open https://www.premierleague.com/en/tables/premier-league to mirror the capture context.
2. First, test the explicit matchweek endpoint by running browser_eval_js with window.fetch to GET:
   "https://sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com/api/v1/competitions/8/seasons/2025/matchweeks/27/matches".
   Do not send any custom headers. Capture status, any CORS errors, and a truncated (~2KB) JSON snippet.
3. Next, test the more generic matches search endpoint via browser_eval_js fetch to:
   "https://sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com/api/v2/matches?compSeasons=719&gameweeks=27&altIds=true&fixtures=true&live=false&page=0&pageSize=40&sort=asc&statuses=C&statuses=U&teams=1&teams=2"
   (use these example params taken from typical usage; if you need compSeasons id, use 719 for PL 2025 as inferred from capture). Again, no custom headers. Capture status, any CORS issues, and a body snippet.
4. If either fetch fails due to CORS, try navigating directly to the failing API URL with browser_navigate and report what the browser shows (raw JSON, error page, etc.). If still blocked, use capture_search_transactions with a query like "matches?compSeasons" or "matchweeks/27/matches" to retrieve the recorded request and, if necessary, use browser_cdp_command (Network.enable + Page.navigate) to replay it and get the JSON.
Return a concise report for both endpoints: which worked, required query parameters, and example response structure (keys only).
arguments.output_description: Confirmation of how to call the Pulselive fixtures endpoints for a specific matchweek, including working URLs, parameter patterns, CORS behavior, and top-level JSON keys.

arguments.usage_guide:
This catalog provides routines for scraping key public APIs behind premierleague.com. Use them from a browser-like context (or any HTTP client that can send standard web headers) against the documented endpoints on api.premierleague.com and sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com.

Routines:
1) pl_standings — Fetch Premier League standings for a competition/season via Pulselive /api/v5/competitions/{competitionId}/seasons/{seasonId}/standings. Use when you need league tables and form breakdowns. Parameters: competitionId (int, e.g. 8 for PL), seasonId (int, e.g. 2025).

2) pl_fixtures_by_matchweek — Fetch fixtures for a given competition, season, and matchweek via Pulselive /api/v1/competitions/{competitionId}/seasons/{seasonId}/matchweeks/{matchweek}/matches or the generic /api/v2/matches with compSeasons, gameweeks, etc. Use when you need match lists or schedules by round.

3) pl_teams_list — Fetch list of teams for a competition/season via Pulselive /api/v1/competitions/{competitionId}/seasons/{seasonId}/teams. Use this first when you need team ids/names to feed into other routines.

4) pl_team_profile_bundle — Given a team id, combine: Pulselive team core (/api/v2/teams/{teamId} or /api/v2/teams-by-id?id={teamId}), metadata (/api/v1/metadata/SDP_FOOTBALL_TEAM/{teamId}), form and next fixture (/api/v1/competitions/{compId}/seasons/{seasonId}/teams/{teamId}/form and /nextfixture), plus promo/content from api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/PROMO/en with references to the team. Use when building a rich team page.

5) pl_player_profile_and_stats — Given playerId and season, call Pulselive /api/v1/players/{playerId} plus /api/v2/competitions/{compId}/seasons/{seasonId}/players/{playerId}/stats. Use for detailed player pages or comparison tools.

6) pl_match_detail — Given matchId, call Pulselive /api/v1/matches/{matchId}/events and /api/v3/matches/{matchId}/lineups. Use for timelines and lineup graphics.

7) pl_content_search — Use api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/en with query parameters (contentTypes, page, pageSize, tagNames, flags) to search articles and videos. Use to surface general PL content.

8) pl_playlist_detail — Use api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/playlist/en/{playlistId} with optional pageSize/detail params to fetch curated content lists. Use for carousels and themed collections.

9) pl_video_detail — Use api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/VIDEO/en/{videoId} to fetch video metadata, and api.premierleague.com/content/premierleague/photo/PHOTO/en/{photoId} for images. Use when embedding media.

10) pl_broadcast_schedule — Use api.premierleague.com/broadcasting/events and /broadcasting/match-events with dateFrom/dateTo, page, pageSize, and sportDataId filters to retrieve TV/broadcast schedules.

All core football-data and content endpoints observed are public GETs with no Authorization or cookies. In a browser, use window.fetch with default headers from a premierleague.com origin to avoid CORS issues; in non-browser clients, mimic a modern browser User-Agent and standard headers. Start with pl_teams_list and pl_standings to discover ids, then chain into team, player, match, and content routines as needed.
